title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0460
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0460
Multiple Vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS
Original Issue Date:September 16, 2026
Severity Rating: CRITICAL
Software Affected
Mikrotik router OS version 7.24 and prior to 7.24.2
Mikrotik router OS version 7.0.0  and prior to 7.23.4
Mikrotik router OS version 6.0.0 and prior to 6.49.21
Overview
Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in MikroTik RouterOS that could allow attackers to escalate privileges, bypass authentication, and cause denial-of-service (DoS) attacks on affected systems.
Target Audience:
All organizations and individuals using MikroTik Router.
Risk Assessment:
High risks of bypass authentication and data breach.
Impact Assessment:
Potential impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the system.
Description
1. Denial of Service Vulnerability
(
CVE-2026-67277
)
A vulnerability exists in MikroTik RouterOS due to a missing authentication check in MikroTik RouterOSs bandwidth-test (btest) service. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted network requests to the exposed btest service.
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to read portions of uninitialized kernel memory and cause the router to crash or restart, resulting in a denial-of-service condition.
2. Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
(
CVE-2026-86060
)
A vulnerability exists in MikroTik RouterOS due to improper handling and neutralization of argument delimiters in the RouterOS SSH login path. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted username or command argument through an accessible SSH login session to alter the RouterOS policy mask.
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to escalate privileges and use the compromised router to access internal systems.
3. Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
(
CVE-2026-67276
)
A vulnerability exists in MikroTik RouterOS due to an incomplete verification of RSA public keys during MikroTik RouterOS SSH authentication. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted SSH public-key authentication request containing a forged RSA key and signature.
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to bypass authentication and potentially gain full administrative control of the targeted system.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned in MikroTik advisory:
https://mikrotik.com/supportsec/september-2026-vulnerability/
